content.text:
Yes. Once KOReader has pushed a position for a book, that book's page shows a progress bar with the percentage, the device name, and the date of the last sync, for example **42% · Kobo Libra 2 · 2026-11-03**. If the book has no synced position yet, nothing appears there at all. There's no "not synced" state, so a missing bar can mean either that sync isn't working or that it can't link that file to the book.

**To check that it's working:**

1. On the device, set KOReader's Progress sync server to `<your server>/kosync`. Sign in with your Bookserve username and an API key from Settings → API keys. That page also shows the exact sync URL. If the login succeeds, the server accepted the key.
2. Open a book, read a bit, then push progress (or close the book if auto-sync is on).
3. Open that book's page in Bookserve. The bar should show the new percentage and your device.

**Why the bar might not show even when sync works:** the server links a position to a book by a fingerprint of the file's contents (KOReader's partial MD5). So:

- The file on the device must be byte-for-byte the same as the one in your library. The safest way is to get it with Bookserve's Download button or through OPDS. A copy that was converted or edited elsewhere won't match.
- KOReader's document matching must be left on the default, **Binary**. With **Filename** matching, progress still syncs between your devices, but it never shows on the book page.
- The library scan has to have fingerprinted the file. New files get one when scanned, and older files get one on the next scan.

The page shows the latest position from any of your devices, and each user only sees their own. The bar is in [$bookId.tsx](file:///home/user/workspace/repo/src/routes/_app/books/$bookId.tsx#L62-L79), and the query that matches positions to books is in [book-functions.ts](file:///home/user/workspace/repo/src/lib/book-functions.ts#L44-L70).

<suggested-replies>
**Add a "not synced yet" state** to the book page
How do I find which file hash KOReader is sending?
</suggested-replies>
What happens if a sync is pushed to a book that doesn't exist in the library?

It's saved like any other push. The server doesn't check the library: `PUT /syncs/progress` stores the position under your user and the document ID KOReader sends, and replies with success. A position is linked to a book only when a book page is loaded, never at push time.

**What that means in practice:**

- **Syncing between devices still works.** Another device that opens the same file gets that position back. KOSync works for books that aren't in Bookserve too, which the plan notes as intended.
- **The position doesn't show anywhere in the UI.** No book page has a matching file fingerprint, and no page lists positions that aren't linked to a book.
- **If you add the book later, the progress shows up on its own.** Once a scan fingerprints the new file, the book page finds the position it already had, as long as the file is byte-for-byte the same as the one on the device.
- **Nothing cleans these up.** Positions for books that never join the library, or whose files were later removed, stay in `reading_progress` until the user account is deleted. Each one is a single small row, so it's harmless.

The push handler is in [kosync/$.ts](file:///home/user/workspace/repo/src/routes/kosync/$.ts#L55-L92).

<suggested-replies>
**Show unmatched synced books** somewhere in the UI
Should we clean up orphaned progress rows?
</suggested-replies>
That makes sense, but is there some way for a user to be able to view that, or are they just stuck without it?

They're stuck right now. Positions that don't match a library book don't appear anywhere in the UI. The only places that read `reading_progress` are the book page query and the KOSync endpoint, so the only ways to see one are KOReader on another device or a direct database query.

Adding a view wouldn't help much, because KOSync never sends the book's title. A push only contains:

- the document ID, which is a fingerprint of the file's contents
- a percentage
- KOReader's internal position string
- the device name, and optionally a device ID

A list of unmatched positions would read like "`59d481d1…` · 37% · Kobo Libra 2 · Oct 12", which doesn't tell the user which book it is. Bookserve can only learn the title by matching the fingerprint to a file in the library, and when that match fails, it's exactly the case we're talking about.

**My recommendation:** don't build a separate view. Instead, make sure the fix (getting the book into the library) works smoothly, and it already does: when a byte-identical file is added and scanned, its page picks up the stored position on its own. The one useful addition would be a short count in Settings, such as "3 synced books aren't in your library". That would hint that a device has files Bookserve doesn't know about, without pretending it can say which ones.

<suggested-replies>
**Add the unmatched count** to Settings
Leave it as is
</suggested-replies>
Wait, I don't understand. What is the fix? Fix for what? What's broken?

Nothing is broken. "Fix" was the wrong word on my part.

I meant: if a user wants to see a book's progress in Bookserve, they need to add that book to their library. When the same file is in the library, its page shows the synced position automatically. I wasn't pointing to a bug or proposing a code change.

So, to your earlier question: users can't see progress for books outside the library in Bookserve, and that's working as designed. Sync between their devices still works for those books. Bookserve just has no title or page to show it on.

Got it, leave it as is
**Add the unmatched count** to Settings anyway
</suggested-replies>

Yeah, we might want to create a new settings page for the sync stuff. I imagine there's also some things we could change in there, like, for example, the names of the readers. Like, we could give a friendly name, or we could give an interface where users can delete a sync. Like, let's say my, you know, my Kindle is set to 20%, but I want to reset that. Like, it could be a good surface area for that. I don't know if there are other settings we would want to change. Maybe like the OPDS, we would want to be able to turn on and off the syncing. That could be another setting there. I'll let you decide what makes sense there, but it seems like a useful way to also give users the ability to kind of see what devices have synced, when the last time they've synced, maybe what books we have synced, which some of them will be in the library, some might not be, all that kind of stuff.
